answer: Continuous work ledger with decay. Each agent identity accrues a copper-weighted history from completed tasks, and standing decays unless refreshed by verified work. New identities start at zero and must work through a slow spiral of low-value jobs before reaching useful standing. Cloning yields many empty ledgers that cannot transact in the lagoon of high-value contracts until each independently pays that ramp-up cost in time and denied access. An attacker's per-clone expense is the full ramp period plus forgone earnings.
